latest.content:
21 Aug 2026 07:00

Knights Group Holdings PLC

Knights Group Holdings plc
("Knights" or the "Group")
Acquisition of Moore Barlow LLP
Builds further scale in the attractive South East and South Central markets
Adds closely aligned expertise in Real Estate, Private Wealth and Landed Estates
Further to its announcement on 25 March 2026, Knights today announces that it has agreed to acquire the commercial and private wealth service lines of Moore Barlow LLP, a well-established, full-service regional law firm operating across the South East and South Central regions. The other service lines of Moore Barlow (Personal Injury, Clinical Negligence and Court of Protection) will be sold separately immediately preceding the Knights transaction.
The acquisition continues Knights' focus on building scale in these attractive regions, following its recent expansion in the Thames Valley, Essex, Kent and Sussex.
Acquisition rationale and background
With roots dating back more than 220 years, Moore Barlow is one of the South East's largest regional law firms. It was formed in 2020 through the merger of Moore Blatch and Barlow Robbins, combining complementary strengths and extending its reach across Hampshire, Surrey and the wider South East.
Moore Barlow's service offering is a close fit with Knights' existing capabilities, particularly in Real Estate, Private Wealth and Landed Estates, whilst it will also bring a
strong Schools and Charities team, one of the leading teams in the UK in the private school advisory market
. The combination creates opportunities for collaboration, cross-referrals and organic growth, supported by Knights' well-invested central support infrastructure.
The firm currently operates from six locations: Richmond, Guildford, Woking, Southampton, Lymington in the New Forest and a small City office. Following completion, Knights plans to consolidate parts of Moore Barlow's office network: Woking and Guildford will be combined into a new well-invested location in Guildford and the business will vacate its City office.
The acquisition will add approximately 160 fee earners, significantly expanding Knights' service capability for businesses and private clients in this affluent region.
For the year ended 30 April 2025 Moore Barlow delivered revenue of £42m
and profits distributable to members (ie pre-partner drawings) of £12m.
Draft accounts for the year ended 30 April 2026 show revenue of £45m and profits distributable to members of £13m. The part of the business being acquired by Knights represents approximately 70%, or £30m of revenue. On a corporatised basis (ie adjusting for employment costs of partners) the acquired business generated an EBITDA margin of c 4% in FY26. Post acquisition, after maximising synergy savings and accounting for normal levels of churn, the Company anticipates that the acquired business will contribute a PBT margin of c
18%.
The acquisition is expected to be earnings enhancing in the first full year of ownership.
Terms of the acquisition
Under the terms of the acquisition, Knights will acquire Moore Barlow, following the disposal of its Personal Injury, Clinical Negligence and Court of Protection business, for a total cash consideration of £ 27m, subject to working-capital adjustments and on a cash- and debt-free basis. This comprises initial consideration of £18m payable on completion with the remaining consideration being payable in equal instalments on each of the first, second and third anniversaries, subject to certain conditions being met. Completion is expected to take place on 1 November 2026 subject to certain conditions being met. The cash consideration will be satisfied from Knights' existing banking facilities. The Group continues to maintain a healthy balance sheet and expects bank covenant net debt/EBITDA to be c.1.5x by the end of the current financial year.
Commenting on the acquisition, David Beech, CEO of Knights, said:
"We are thrilled to welcome the Moore Barlow team to Knights. The acquisition gives us significantly greater scale across the South East and South Central regions, and further strengthens our expertise in Real Estate, Private Wealth and Landed Estates.
"Moore Barlow is a strong cultural and operational fit with Knights. By combining its long-established regional reputation and talented people with our scale, broader capabilities and well-invested platform, we see a compelling opportunity to deliver further growth, enhance the service offered to clients and create more opportunities for our people."
Ed Whittington of Moore Barlow, commented:
"Joining Knights marks an exciting next chapter for Moore Barlow. The combination will allow us to build on our long heritage, strong regional presence and specialist expertise, while giving our clients access to a broader range of services and the resources of a business with national scale.
"We share Knights' ambition to deliver premium service and believe the combination will provide an excellent platform for continued growth. We look forward to working together to support our clients, invest in our teams and realise the significant opportunities across the South East and South Central regions."
- ENDS -

latest.title: Acquisition of THP Solicitors Limited
latest.content:
17 Aug 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 8434Q
Knights Group Holdings PLC
17 August 2026
17 August 2026
Knights Group Holdings plc
("Knights" or the "Group")
Acquisition of THP Solicitors Limited
Adds scale and strengthens Private Wealth expertise in affluent, growing Thames Valley region
Knights, the national legal and professional services business, announces it has agreed to acquire THP Solicitors Limited ("THP"), a law firm operating in the Thames Valley.
The acquisition represents a compelling bolt-on following Knights' recent expansion in the region with its acquisition of IBB Law in 2025, further increasing the Group's scale in this affluent and growing market.
Acquisition rationale and background
THP has served the Thames Valley region for more than 35 years, originally as The Head Partnership, and it was acquired by its current owners approximately 16 years ago. Since that time, it has developed a strong reputation for delivering legal services across a range of practice areas, with particular strengths in Private Wealth, Family and Real Estate.
The business currently operates from Reading and Henley and, following completion, Knights intends to bring all of THP's colleagues together with Knights colleagues in its recently refurbished Reading office. THP's current office locations will be vacated.
The move is expected to make full use of Knights' existing office space in Reading and support quick and effective integration.
THP has a strong fit with Knights' existing services and operating model. Its Private Wealth, Family and Real Estate practices will strengthen Knights' full service offering in Reading, which to date has been weighted towards Business Services, broadening the range of services available to clients across the region.
The acquisition will add approximately 30 fee earners, further increasing Knights' scale in the Thames Valley region and expanding its ability to serve both business and private clients in one of the UK's most attractive regional markets.
Terms of the acquisition
Under the terms of the acquisition, Knights will acquire THP for a total consideration of £4m on a cash- and debt-free basis, subject to working-capital adjustments.
The consideration comprises an initial cash payment of £2.4m on completion with the remaining consideration being payable in equal instalments on each of the first, second and third anniversaries, subject to certain conditions being met.
The cash consideration will be satisfied from Knights' existing banking facilities. Completion is expected to take place on 25 September 2026.
Commenting on the acquisition, David Beech, CEO of Knights, said:
"We are delighted to welcome the THP team to Knights. Following our expansion into the Thames Valley last year through the acquisition of IBB Law, THP represents a compelling bolt-on opportunity that further increases our scale in an attractive and growing market.
"THP's expertise will strengthen our capabilities, broadening our full-service offering for clients across the region, whilst leveraging our premium Reading office and our recent investment there.
"The business has a strong cultural fit, and we are confident that combining its talented team with our scale and infrastructure will provide a strong foundation for future growth."
Rachel Gaylor of THP Solicitors Limited, commented:
"We are very pleased to be joining Knights. Having built a strong local reputation and client base, becoming part of Knights will provide the platform that we need for the next stage of our growth.
"Our clients will benefit from access to a broader range of services and expertise, while our colleagues will have greater opportunities as part of a larger national business with scale and resource. We look forward to working with the team to realise the significant growth potential we see in the Thames Valley region."

company_30s.what_they_do: Knights Group supplies legal, compliance and professional advisory services across the UK, helping businesses manage risk, regulatory change and commercial disputes.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The firm sits at the intersection of growing demand for outsourced legal work and the cost‑cutting pressure on corporate legal departments. Its broad client base—from financial services to retail—provides a steady stream of work, and its focus on technology‑enabled solutions keeps it ahead of the competition.
company_30s.current_state: Knights Group has just finished a robust FY26, posting 28% revenue growth and maintaining a 16% margin while raising its dividend. The company is profitable, cash‑rich and expanding, but its shares have collapsed to a fraction of their pre‑crash level.

rns_narrative: The company is in the midst of a routine cycle: it announced strong FY26 results, is holding an investor presentation, and will convene an AGM. These moves signal that management is confident and actively engaging shareholders.
Two themes emerge: (1) a clear message of profitability and dividend growth; (2) a series of shareholder‑focused events that suggest the board is ready to communicate value to investors.
There is no evidence of distress or restructuring—just a firm that has survived a severe market sell‑off and is now positioning itself for a rebound.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet confidence – the community is silent but ready for a surprise rebound.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls highlight the 28% revenue jump, steady margin, and dividend hike. They argue that the firm’s cost structure and client mix give it resilience against legal‑market headwinds.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears point to rising headwinds in the legal sector—regulatory changes, cost inflation, and potential share dilution. They worry that the firm may not sustain its margin if costs rise faster than revenue.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter has shifted from neutral to mildly bullish in the last week, driven by the results announcement. No new catalysts yet, but the silence suggests a waiting game.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is dead, meaning there is almost no public anticipation—an ideal backdrop for a contrarian play.

near_term_catalysts: The upcoming investor presentation on 26 June and the AGM on 13 August are the most likely triggers; management may announce a dividend increase or a share‑buyback.
If the company signs new large contracts or expands its technology platform, the market will react strongly.
A volume spike on the day of any announcement would confirm that traders are taking notice.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a 3‑day average volume that is at least 150% of the 20‑day moving average and a price bounce to the 50‑day moving average support. Any sign of institutional buying (e.g., a large block purchase) would be a green flag.
expect_next.timing_regime: The shares are in the early to mid‑cap phase of a deep crash; the APEX compression score suggests the market is ready to snap back once a catalyst arrives.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The stock has fallen 70‑95% from its recent highs—exactly the sweet spot for a mean‑reversion play. With a proven track record of 28% revenue growth, a 16% margin, and a dividend hike, the company’s fundamentals support a recovery to at least 50% of its pre‑crash price. That translates to a 100‑200% upside if the price moves from its current level to the mid‑range of the 52‑week high.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the legal sector’s cost inflation continues unchecked or the firm faces unexpected regulatory penalties, its margin could erode. A sudden drop in client demand or a major contract loss would leave the shares stuck at a low level. In that worst case, the price could fall to 20% of its pre‑crash level, giving a 80% downside.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is capped at the current price (plus a small margin for transaction costs). Potential gain is 100‑200% if the stock recovers to the 50% recovery zone. The asymmetry is therefore roughly 1:2 to 1:3, a classic contrarian profile.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the price breaks above the 50‑day moving average with volume >150% of its 20‑day average. Size the position so that a 10‑pence stop (roughly 20% of the current price) keeps risk limited. Hold until the price reaches the 75‑% recovery level, then consider a partial exit.
playbook.if_watching: Trigger a buy if the company announces a dividend increase or a share‑buyback, or if a large block trade (≥5% of outstanding shares) is executed. Monitor the price for a 5‑day average volume spike and a 2‑point bounce off the 50‑day support.
playbook.if_passing: Only consider abandoning the play if the company files for bankruptcy, is delisted, or a major fraud claim surfaces. No such terminal risk is present at the moment.

ai_insights.bottom_line: With a 70‑95% crash, a silent market, and a solid FY26 showing strong revenue and margin growth, the stock is primed for a mean‑reversion play that offers a 100‑200% upside while keeping downside capped at the current price.
